title: Botched install caused installer to stop because it thinks it is installed.

judgment.rationale: The failure matches an existing fork-side installer condition fix and related upstream reports; no competing design should be created.
evidence: The installer reports 0x81f40001 after a botched uninstall.
The issue discussion identifies stale files/registration and inability to reproduce elsewhere.
Fork commit bc74079a3 changes both cross-scope conditions to allow maintenance when WixBundleInstalled is true.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify the existing fork fix against the stale-registration scenario and request installer evidence only if the fix does not cover it.

fix_assessment.rationale: An active fork fix changes the relevant PowerToysSetupVNext cross-scope conditions; do not invent a competing plan.

issue_context.summary: A botched uninstall leaves installer registration that blocks reinstall with 0x81f40001 even though the application is absent.
known_information: The reporter cannot install any version after a failed uninstall.
The user supplied the exact error and says files remain.
Related reports identify the same stale-installation state.
The fork contains a condition-level fix.
inferences: Stale per-user/per-machine product registration is likely being treated as a blocking installation.
Allowing maintenance for an installed bundle may make cleanup reachable.
issue_context.analysis: Because a concrete fork fix already covers the likely bootstrapper gate, the correct workflow is validation of that fix rather than a duplicate design.
initial_investigation: Inspected PowerToysSetupVNext PowerToys.wxs and Product.wxs detection/condition paths and checked related issue history.
Confirmed no safe basis for broad registry cleanup.

information_gaps.information: Installer log or exact detected product scope/version.
information_gaps.why_needed: Confirms whether the existing cross-scope condition is the path hit by this report.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Run the installer with verbose logging on the affected machine and attach only the relevant public log excerpt.

comment.body: The 0x81f40001 symptom and remaining files match a known stale-installation path, and a fork-side installer condition fix already covers maintenance for an installed bundle. To confirm it applies to your machine, please share the installer log's detected PowerToys product scope/version and the exact step where the condition fails. Do not remove unrelated registry entries.
